items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I think the boogie-woogie pianist, Pete Johnson, Albert Hammond, maybe Leadbelly was on there.

ctx.x: And he did the same thing in 1936 with the Goodman Trio. And Goodman went along with it, you know, and a lot of those people at MCA were telling Goodman, you're a young man coming up and you're a great clarinet player and you start this racial mix and you're gonna stop

your career before you ever get started.
But it just so happened it was the other way around. Hammond was right. Goodman became one of the most successful musicians financially in the business because of the race thing. The tremendous spotlight of pioneering. And then after that, everybody began mixing -- Billie Holiday joined Artie Shaw's band and Charlie Shavers joined Tommy Dorsey.
Well, we're jumping the guns here a bit -- I want to get you out of Chicago now. I remember, because I knew you in Chicago.
